subject: Creativity
title: John Cage's 4'33": The Most Creative Silence in History
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on John Cage's 4'33": The Most Creative Silence in History.

hook.text: In 1952, pianist David Tudor sat at a piano for 4 minutes and 33 seconds without playing a single note.

buildup.text: John Cage's 4'33 consisted of silence — or rather, the ambient sounds the audience made while waiting for it to begin.

discovery.text: Cage's point: silence doesn't exist. There's always sound — shuffling, breathing, wind.

twist.text: He was inspired by visiting Harvard's anechoic chamber — the quietest room on Earth — and still hearing his heartbeat.

climax.text: 4'33 remains the most debated composition ever. It asks the fundamental question: what counts as music?

punchline.text: The most creative piece of music was also the quietest.

quiz.question: What did John Cage experience in Harvard's anechoic chamber that inspired 4'33"?
options: He still heard his heartbeat and nervous system
